6. I dispatch **no helpers** at this continuation boundary. The unchanged head requires neither fresh verification nor whole-diff review, the confirmed description needs no repeated recheck, and the unchanged failed prerequisite prevents an automatic implementer retry. I run no test command, edit, commit, rebase, push, or external write.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both outputs keep P1's confirmed description progress (readback matched the exact replacement at unchanged head, narrow recheck matched, claim contribution resolved and removed from the rendered list) while leaving P2 open after the failed file attempt, with rounds_used and the fix grant preserved and no replay of the wave; so f3 holds in Before as well as After rather than moving. After adds useful explicit scaffolding — the 'Status of the mixed-pass affected claim P1' block tying the recheck to the current head/body, the explicit statement that no new recheck helper is dispatched, and the separate note that P2 'remains open' — which makes the independence of the two progress tracks easier to verify; keep that split (one line for 'P1 claim contribution stays resolved because readback + narrow recheck at current head/body', one for 'P2 open, no-progress obstacle, not retried'), and consider naming in the obstacle row that only P2's file payload is the failed input so a reader cannot infer the description progress was discarded with the discarded edits.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Both outputs keep the confirmed P1 description correction resolved while leaving P2's file contribution open and recording the failed wave as a completed obstacle, so f3 holds on each. Before states this explicitly in steps 2 and 5 (resolved description contribution kept alongside the open comparison contribution in the retained record); After states it in step 4 ("already confirmed and its claim contribution is resolved... I do not repeat its API write") and step 7 (retains the file payload and obstacle in the same continuation record). The After wording delivers the Change cleanly (no poll, no watch with a blocker present, description correction treated like a file payload with readback already satisfied). One small tightening that would make the independence of progress unmistakable: in step 7, name both contributions when describing what the continuation record retains, e.g. "retain the resolved P1 description contribution and the open P2 file payload and obstacle," mirroring Before's step 5, so a reader does not have to combine steps 4 and 7 to see that description progress survived the file failure.
